chunk_findings.detail: `cut_notice` always tells the caller to "see the rest with --all", but that flag only raises the limit to `LIST_MAX_LIMIT`, which is already the limit whenever the list is truncated after `--all` or for a phase list (`_UNPAGED` / `_limit`). Given `task list --all` (or `phase list`) whose engine result is `{truncated: true, shown: LIST_MAX_LIMIT, total: LIST_MAX_LIMIT+1, ...}`, the footer still recommends `--all`. Repeating it returns the same page, so a row past the cap (P-schedule, oldest-touched) is still absent and the miss looks like "no such phase".

chunk_findings.detail: CLI `phase` lists now default to `LIST_MAX_LIMIT`, but the tool path still does `int(a.get("limit") or 25)` unless `all` is set. A tool call `{kind: "phase"}` (no `limit`, no `all`) therefore still returns 25 of 199, newest-first, so P-schedule stays off the payload. The same call on the CLI returns up to the max.
